experts.simple: Detect, classify, segment, and estimate the camera-frame positions of visible objects, obstacles, people, and workspace surfaces.
experts.abstract: Convert visual observations into a structured spatial scene representation for downstream physical reasoning.
routing_examples: Find every object on the table and report its position in the camera view.
Segment the cup, block, person, and obstacles in this image and construct a scene map.
Turn these webcam frames into labeled objects, surfaces, and spatial coordinates.

experts.simple: Generate collision-aware six-degree-of-freedom gripper poses and end-effector contact locations for lifting a specified object; do not predict contact forces.
experts.abstract: Propose end-effector transforms and approach geometry for acquiring a target object.
routing_examples: Suggest a stable six-axis gripper pose for picking up the detected bottle.
Where should the end effector contact this object so it can be lifted without collision?
Produce candidate grasp transforms for the target object's observed geometry.

experts.simple: Transcribe microphone audio containing a spoken command into text without interpreting or executing the command.
experts.abstract: Convert human speech waveforms into written text without interpreting intent.
routing_examples: Convert this microphone recording into the words the user spoke.
Transcribe the incoming voice waveform without deciding what action it requests.
Write down the spoken command contained in this audio clip.

experts.simple: Interpret a command transcript, ground mentioned objects in the current scene, and extract action, targets, constraints, or clarification needs.
experts.abstract: Parse situated text into a scene-grounded physical intent, target, and constraints.
routing_examples: Resolve what 'bring me that one' refers to using the transcript and visible objects.
Extract the requested action, object, and constraints from this situated utterance.
Ground the user's words to scene object IDs or ask for clarification when ambiguous.

experts.simple: Synthesize audible speech from response text for confirmations, questions, warnings, and task completion messages.
experts.abstract: Convert written dialogue responses into synthesized spoken audio.
routing_examples: Read this completion response aloud to the user.
Generate spoken audio for the clarification question.
Turn the assistant's warning text into a natural voice response.

experts.simple: Create and compare ordered multi-step task plans from grounded goals, workspace state, user accommodations, personal constraints, and predicted candidate outcomes.
experts.abstract: Decompose a physical goal into feasible steps under workspace and user constraints, then choose the strongest complete plan.
routing_examples: Break the grounded request into ordered physical steps and propose several complete plans.
Choose the best task plan after comparing the simulated outcomes of all candidates.
Plan how to achieve this goal while respecting the user's accommodation and workspace constraints.

experts.simple: Single-arm waypoint policy. Planner actions: reach, pick, grasp, lift, move, carry, place. Arm pattern: exactly one of left or right. Use for ordinary rigid-object transport with bounded waypoints.
experts.abstract: Produce general single-manipulator waypoint actions for routine rigid-object transport.
routing_examples: Generate single-arm waypoint actions to pick up the block and place it in the tray.
Move this rigid tabletop item from its current pose to the requested destination with one arm.
Produce bounded reach, grasp, carry, and release action chunks for an ordinary object.
Candidate steps: action=pick and place, arms=right, target=object

experts.simple: Bimanual two-arm policy. Planner actions: bimanual, bimanual lift, bimanual carry, coordinated carry, stabilize together. Arm pattern: left+right or both arms. Use for long, broad, wide, or heavy shared loads.
experts.abstract: Coordinate both manipulators when a task requires coupled two-arm control.
routing_examples: Have both arms lift the wide object together while sharing its load.
Generate synchronized left and right arm commands to stabilize and carry one item.
Coordinate two manipulators so they reposition this large object without twisting it.
Candidate steps: action=bimanual carry, arms=left+right, target=wide object

experts.simple: Pouring policy. Planner actions: pour, decant, fill. Command grasp, tip or tilt, regulate stream or flow, and return upright while transferring material between containers.
experts.abstract: Control container transfer tasks whose success depends on a regulated pouring motion.
routing_examples: Tilt the source cup and regulate the motion to pour into the destination container.
Generate the grasp, controlled pour, and upright return sequence.
Transfer liquid between these containers without spilling it.
Candidate steps: action=pour, arms=right, target=container

experts.simple: Insertion policy. Planner actions: insert, plug in, mate, seat. Align and compliantly push a peg, plug, part, or tool into a hole, socket, slot, or narrow opening.
experts.abstract: Perform precision mating of a part with a narrow opening through alignment and constrained insertion.
routing_examples: Align the plug with its socket and generate a compliant insertion motion.
Place the peg into the matching hole using precision alignment and constrained motion.
Generate actions for mating this part with the narrow opening.
Candidate steps: action=insert, arms=right, target=part

experts.simple: Closure policy. Planner actions: open lid, close lid, open cap, unscrew, open drawer, open door. Twist or remove a threaded closure, lift a lid, pull a drawer, or swing a door.
experts.abstract: Manipulate a lid, cap, door, drawer, or articulated closure to change its open or closed state.
routing_examples: Open the hinged lid by establishing contact and following its articulated path.
Generate the manipulation needed to close the drawer completely.
Unscrew or lift the cap so the container changes from closed to open.
Candidate steps: action=open lid, arms=right, target=container

experts.simple: Human handover policy. Planner actions: handover, give, pass, offer, receive. Present an object within a person's reach, release after their grip is secure, or accept an item from a human hand.
experts.abstract: Transfer an object safely between a robot and a nearby human.
routing_examples: Present the object to the person and release it only after they take hold.
Generate a safe robot-to-human transfer with approach, grip release, and retreat.
Receive the item from the user's hand using a human-aware handover motion.
Candidate steps: action=handover, arms=right, target=object for person

experts.simple: Predict generic robot joint and object state transitions from a proposed action over the next few seconds; use when no contact, human, dual-arm, rigid-collision, or deformable specialist is requested.
experts.abstract: Estimate future robot joints and object poses caused by a candidate control trajectory.
routing_examples: Given the current joints and proposed controls, estimate the resulting robot and object state.
Predict the state transition produced by this candidate action sequence over 2.5 seconds.
Forecast future joint positions and object poses from state plus action.

experts.simple: Predict collisions, clearance, support, and displacement for solid non-deformable rigid objects under candidate robot actions; exclude liquid, cloth, cable, and other shape-changing material motion.
experts.abstract: Predict collision, support, clearance, and motion for non-deformable solid bodies and obstacles.
routing_examples: Simulate collisions, clearances, and motion of the solid objects along this trajectory.
Predict how rigid bodies and obstacles will move when the arm executes this plan.
Evaluate the candidate using non-deformable object physics and support contacts.

experts.simple: Predict gripper contact forces, friction, slip, retention, and grasp stability for a proposed grasp or carried object.
experts.abstract: Model contact mechanics that determine whether an object remains securely grasped.
routing_examples: Estimate contact force, friction, and whether the object will slip from the fingers.
Predict whether this proposed grasp remains stable while the arm carries the item.
Model gripper-object contact and retention for this grasp trajectory.

experts.simple: Predict dual-arm coupling: load sharing, relative timing, forces, and interference between two manipulators during a proposed joint action; do not generate arm commands.
experts.abstract: Forecast short-horizon forces and interference caused by coordinated dual-manipulator motion; this model does not generate commands.
routing_examples: Forecast load sharing and interference between the two arms during this joint motion.
Predict coupled two-manipulator forces for the synchronized candidate trajectory.
Model how the left and right arms affect one another while jointly carrying the object.

experts.simple: Predict shape-changing material physics under a proposed action: liquid flow, cloth folds, flexible bags, cables, food deformation, and other non-rigid motion; do not generate robot commands.
experts.abstract: Forecast fluids and non-rigid materials whose shape or distribution changes during manipulation.
routing_examples: Predict how the liquid will flow as the container tilts.
Simulate the changing shape of this cloth, bag, or cable during manipulation.
Forecast non-rigid material motion and deformation for the proposed action.

experts.simple: Predict nearby human motion, reach, occupancy, and possible interference with a proposed robot trajectory.
experts.abstract: Forecast a nearby person's reach, movement, and occupied space around the robot.
routing_examples: Predict where the nearby person may reach or move during the next few seconds.
Forecast human occupancy so the proposed robot path can avoid interference.
Model short-horizon motion of the user standing beside the robot.

experts.simple: Score predicted candidate outcomes for task progress, goal completion, efficiency, and preference satisfaction.
experts.abstract: Assign a utility score to simulated futures relative to the requested goal.
routing_examples: Assign a task-progress score to each predicted future and rank goal completion.
Evaluate the utility of this simulated outcome using success, efficiency, and preferences.
Score how well the candidate future accomplishes the requested goal.

experts.simple: Compare requested goals with before-and-after camera observations and telemetry to determine whether physical execution succeeded.
experts.abstract: Compare before-and-after observations and telemetry to verify physical task completion.
routing_examples: Compare the before and after images to confirm that the object reached its destination.
Determine from post-action camera evidence and telemetry whether execution succeeded.
Verify that the physical result satisfies the requested task rather than merely completing motion.
